key_insight: A symbolic-neural ensemble can recover interpretable interatomic potentials that match DFT accuracy while improving robustness beyond any single learned functional form.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to transparent, physics-based force fields for fast materials simulation, balancing accuracy, transferability, and interpretability.
method: Train EqNN symbolic models for Al using DFT data under three protocols: random init + MCTS + gradient descent, transfer from Cu + MCTS + gradient descent, and transfer from Cu + gradient descent only.
Compare the resulting symbolic minima across phonons, surface energies, elastic response, equation-of-state curvature, and melting behavior.
Combine the complementary models with a weighted symbolic ensemble to reduce bias and improve overall fidelity.
evidence_signal: All three symbolic models achieve sub-10 meV/atom accuracy, and the ensemble further improves agreement with DFT across equilibrium and non-equilibrium benchmarks.
watch_item: The ensemble depends on careful model selection and weighting, and its transferability outside the tested aluminum regimes may require additional validation.
paper_title: Symbolic Ensemble Learning Enables Discovery of Fast Accurate Physics-Based Interatomic Potentials
